name: PeekYou
tip: People search that links names to social media profiles. Fill in your first and last name, email, city and state, do the CAPTCHA, tick the required boxes and tap Submit. Nothing is removed until you tap the link in their email. They say about 10 days.

name: OfficialUSA
tip: Tap FIND ME ON THIS SITE to see its records for your name. If one is you, open the opt-out page, enter your email, pick your record and tap Remove. They say most records go within 48 hours. Its sister site Xlek needs its own opt-out. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: Xlek (sister site of OfficialUSA)
tip: Search your first and last name on this page, tap the result that is you and choose opt-out. Each result needs its own request. They check every request by hand and say it can take up to 30 days. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: SearchBug
tip: Search your name and state on the site. On the record that is you, tap Remove near the top right, tick the box, type the security code shown and tap Remove. They say it takes up to 72 hours. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: Kiwi Searches
tip: Search your name on the site. If a profile is you, open it and copy its link, then come back and tap SEND EMAIL REQUEST. The app puts the copied link in the email. They say about 5 business days. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: Persopo (also People-search.org)
tip: Persopo takes removal requests by email. Search your name, city and state on the site. If a listing is you, copy its link if you can, then tap SEND EMAIL REQUEST. This also clears People-search.org, which Persopo owns. They say 10 to 20 business days. If nothing there is you, tap NOT LISTED.

name: StateRecords.org
tip: Run by the InfoTracer company, but it has its own opt-out. Search your name and location, select every result that is you, enter your email and submit. Answer any questions it asks, then tap the link they email you. They say 24 to 48 hours.

name: CourtRecords.us (and its 50 state sites)
tip: One request covers CourtRecords.us and its 50 state court-records sites. Tap I Agree, enter your first name, last name, state and city and tap Submit. Tick Select Record on the row that is you (check the age and addresses), then tap Request to Remove my Data. Answer any questions before you close the page.

name: BlockShopper (home sales)
tip: Publishes who bought and sold homes. If you have bought or sold a home, search your name on the site. If you are there, copy that page's link and tap SEND EMAIL REQUEST: the link goes in the email, which cites Texas privacy law as they require. If you are not there, tap NOT LISTED.

name: Arity (Allstate driving data)
tip: Allstate's driving-data company. Texas sued it in 2025 for collecting drivers' data through phone apps without telling them. Fill in the form with your email and phone number, plus your phone's advertising ID if you still have one, then submit.

name: Unacast (location data, now with Gravy Analytics)
tip: Location data company that merged with Gravy Analytics. Fill in the opt-out and delete form, adding your phone's advertising ID if you still have one. If the form will not work, tap SEND EMAIL REQUEST instead.

name: Mobilewalla (location data)
tip: Location data company. Its form needs your phone's advertising ID (in Settings, search for Ads). If you deleted that ID after the Kochava step, they have nothing to match, so tap NOT LISTED. Otherwise pick your requests, enter your email and the ID, tick the boxes and tap Process Request.

name: Dun & Bradstreet (business data)
tip: The oldest business-data company. It sells contact details for people tied to businesses. Ask to delete your data and to opt out of its sale, fill in your details and submit, then follow any email they send.

name: Verizon (if it is your carrier)
tip: Verizon uses your browsing and app data for ads under Custom Experience and Custom Experience Plus. Sign in and turn both off. In the My Verizon app it is under Me, Profile & Settings, My Profile. Or call 866-211-0874 and press 2. If Verizon is not your carrier, tap NOT LISTED.

name: AT&T and Cricket (if it is your carrier)
tip: No sign-in needed. Tick both boxes: opt out of sharing and selling, and opt out of the Personalized program. Fill in your name, email, phone and address and tap Submit. Or call 866-385-3193. If AT&T or Cricket is not your carrier, tap NOT LISTED.

name: T-Mobile and Metro (if it is your carrier)
tip: Sign in to the Privacy Dashboard, choose Manage Do Not Sell or Share and slide the toggles to OFF. Turn off any advertising sharing toggles you see there too. If T-Mobile or Metro is not your carrier, tap NOT LISTED.

name: Do Not Call Registry (sales calls)
tip: The government's free list that tells telemarketers to stop calling you. Register your cell number, then tap the link they email you to finish. It never expires. Sales calls should stop within 31 days. Scammers ignore it, but legal sellers must obey it.

name: Google: clear results for removed listings
tip: Use this after a site removes you but Google still shows the old result. Copy that result's link, paste it here and submit. Google checks the page and drops the stale result. Tap MARK AS DONE once you have sent every link you found.

name: Bing: clear results for removed listings
tip: The same clean-up for Bing. Sign in with a Microsoft account, choose Remove Outdated Cache, paste the old result's link and submit. Tap MARK AS DONE once you have sent every link you found.

name: Google: personalized ads off
tip: Stops Google using your activity to target ads on Google and on partner sites and apps. Sign in, set Personalized ads to Off and confirm. It applies to every device where you are signed in.
